findings.reason: The protected function is concise, idiomatic expert-interview Python. vowels names the fixed exclusion set directly, character is precise inside the generator, and join constructs the immutable result once without manual index state or repeated concatenation. There is no unnecessary abstraction or obscured control flow, so a candidate would be cosmetic rather than material.

The generator examines every character exactly once from left to right and yields it exactly when it is not one of a, e, i, o, or u. Consequently every specified vowel is removed, every lowercase consonant including y is retained once, and retained order is unchanged. join returns the empty string for an all-vowel input and an equal string value for a vowel-free input.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode algorithm problem 1119, Python/Python 3, and Solution.removeVowels. Authenticated source evidence confirms the exact five vowels, new-string result, length interval 1 through 1000, and lowercase-English-only input domain. The app-local solve(s) preserves that contract exactly.

The protected solve body and immutable native method bound to verified submission 2067728718 have identical executable statements: the same five-element set and the same generator expression, exclusion predicate, left-to-right source iteration, and join. Their only differences are the app function versus native class wrapper, native annotation, and app module docstring.

The unchanged hidden tiers grow through 64, 256, and 1000 all-vowel characters, forcing complete filtering and repeated immutable copies in the slower control. The protected query passed at a 0.99x largest runtime ratio and -0.01 relative growth exponent. An independently correct repeated-single-removal control preserved every output and failed only scaling at 3.11x and +0.26, distinguishing one-pass construction from quadratic repeated copying.

All eight ordinary fixtures are visible samples or trials. They cover a mixed string, all five vowels, no vowels including y, both one-character outcomes, alternating vowel/consonant positions, repeated vowel runs, stable retained order, and the exact maximum length of 1000.
